title: 1. Trade assembly parameter-search depth for structural breadth
hypothesis: Independent assembly structures escape shared placement-topology errors more efficiently than deeper parameter search within one structure.

prediction.rationale: Compare four structures with six candidates each against one structure with 24 candidates, holding simulator search budget fixed; +0.20 is a useful gain over another unsuccessful search.

code_changes: Reuse existing suites and rollout_search; expose the assembly_breadth_depth study through the command shown. Generate five independent single-phase structures: one depth control and four breadth candidates. Unlike D-020's full-depth independent repeats, this tests allocation between topology coverage and parameter depth at equal episode cost.

Freeze a shared five-case probe and disjoint 30-case promotion manifest before generation. Search 24 candidates for depth and six per breadth structure, including each initial vector; select one winner per arm using only the probe. Evaluate both winners on identical promotion cases and report the paired t interval. Conclusions are conditional on these five structures, not generator-wide estimates.

Use generation seeds 3500-3504, manifest seeds 3505-3506, and search root 3507. Keep bc_steps=0 and gpt-6.1-sol/high/temperature=1. Permit no replacement generation calls; invalid slots remain failures. Require per-idea user approval and stop the remote box afterward.

falsified_by: A paired interval upper bound below +0.20 refutes the predicted gain. An interval containing zero is inconclusive about an advantage; tied success is not improvement.
